record.paper_title: Survey of solved and open problems in the degeneracy phenomenon
record.context_brief: Effect of removing weakly redundant constraints on sensitivity and shadow prices
record.original_question: If primal degeneracy in a linear program is caused by weakly redundant constraints passing through a degenerate optimal vertex x⁰, can one safely omit those weakly redundant constraints and then compute right-hand-side sensitivity ranges or shadow prices in the usual way without changing the correct answer?

evidence.quote: If degeneracy is caused by w. redundancy would then this circumstance not simplify sensitivity analysis and the determination of shadow prices?

We found that in the case of sensitivity analysis with respect to b and shadow prices it is not possible to omit the w. redundant constraints and then determine the shadow price or the parameter interval in the usual sense. We proved [14] that omitting the w. redundant constraints leads to false results in general. This is not true for sensitivity analysis with respect to c.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a linear program in standard form
   maximize  c^T x   subject to  A x ≤ b,  x ≥ 0,
where A is an m×n real matrix, b ∈ ℝ^m, c ∈ ℝ^n. Let x⁰ be an optimal basic feasible solution that is primal-degenerate, meaning that more than n of the constraints (including the nonnegativity constraints) are active at x⁰. A constraint a_i^T x ≤ b_i is called weakly redundant for the feasible region P = {x : Ax ≤ b, x ≥ 0} if it is satisfied with equality at some feasible point but its removal does not change P. Suppose the degeneracy at x⁰ is caused exclusively by weakly redundant constraints passing through x⁰ (i.e., removing all such weakly redundant constraints from the system leaves x⁰ as a non-degenerate optimal vertex of the reduced LP).

Question: Is it true that, for every such linear program, one obtains the correct right-hand-side sensitivity intervals (the ranges of b_i over which the current optimal basis remains optimal) and the correct shadow prices (dual variables associated with the constraints) by deleting the weakly redundant constraints and then performing the standard sensitivity / shadow-price computation on the reduced LP? Equivalently, does omitting weakly redundant constraints preserve the true b-sensitivity ranges and shadow prices of the original LP?
artifact.category_tag: Linear programming degeneracy and sensitivity analysis
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved negatively: in general, omitting weakly redundant constraints that cause degeneracy at an optimal vertex leads to incorrect right-hand-side sensitivity ranges and incorrect shadow prices, although it does not affect sensitivity analysis with respect to the objective coefficients c. This was established in the literature on the degeneracy phenomenon in linear programming (Greenberg; Gal and collaborators).

status_evidence.title: Survey of solved and open problems in the degeneracy phenomenon (zbMATH entry)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses that omitting weakly redundant constraints leads to false results for b-sensitivity and shadow prices in general, while it is acceptable for c-sensitivity.
status_evidence.claim: The negative answer for b-sensitivity and shadow prices, and positive answer for c-sensitivity, is reported as proved.
